Fixes bug Bfa70532c4f: Core tools/list is 40261 bytes against the CORE_BUDGET ratchet (40000) in tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py and tests/test_mcp_tool_tiers.py, so test_sizes_core_under_budget_standard_between and test_tools_list_bytes_per_tier_are_reported fail on main. Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bfa70532c4f --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bfa70532c4f --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug Bfa70532c4f: MCP core tier tools/list over budget ratchet (again)

data.text: Raise the MCP tool core tier budget so the ratchet stops failing (operator authorized this raise). Raise CORE_BUDGET to 50000 (25% headroom), add a one-line comment noting the operator raise (date 2026-11-08, reason = accumulated new tools), ensure the two assertions referencing CORE_BUDGET still pass, run affected tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py scoped unit_tests BEFORE merge, cross-family review (grok/x.ai + gemini/google), merge, complete --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813-Godzila.

data.claim: Raising CORE_BUDGET from 40000 to 50000 in tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py and tests/test_mcp_tool_tiers.py makes the failing ratchet tests pass
data.falsifier: core tools/list would have to exceed 50000 bytes for the ratchet tests to still fail after the raise
data.mechanism: core tools/list is 40261 bytes, so 40261 > 40000 (old ratchet) fails but 40261 <= 50000 (new ratchet) passes
data.probe: uv run pytest tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py tests/test_mcp_tool_tiers.py tests/test_kind_data_surface.py -q --timeout=300
data.question: Does raising CORE_BUDGET to 50000 stop the core-tier ratchet failing?

chunk_findings.detail: The change removes the operator-raised local `CORE_BUDGET = 50_000` and imports `CORE_BUDGET` from `tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py`, but this change does not modify that file — the manifest contains only `tests/test_mcp_tool_tiers.py`, with no new files. Since the failing ratchet in `tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py` is described as `40_000`, the imported `CORE_BUDGET` is still `40_000`, not `50_000`. With the reported core `tools/list` size of 40_261 bytes, `_size(...) > CORE_BUDGET` remains true, so `test_sizes_core_under_budget_standard_between` and `test_tools_list_bytes_per_tier_are_reported` still fail. The actual raise to 50_000 needs to happen in `tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py`, or this file must retain its local 50_000 constant.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_tool_tiers.py:19 (`from tests.test_mcp_tool_budget import CORE_BUDGET`)

chunk_findings.detail: The fix never raises the ratchet. This diff deletes the local `CORE_BUDGET = 50_000` and binds the tiers test to `tests.test_mcp_tool_budget.CORE_BUDGET`, and that module is not in the change. The bug states that module’s ratchet is still 40000 while core `tools/list` is 40261 bytes. After this import, `test_tools_list_bytes_per_tier_are_reported` compares 40261 to 40000 and fails again — the same overage the operator authorized fixing by setting the budget to 50000.

Running `pytest tests/test_mcp_tool_tiers.py::test_tools_list_bytes_per_tier_are_reported` then compares the 40,261-byte core tools/list against 40,000, so the test fails where it previously passed with the removed 50,000 constant; the bug fix is not actually made.
